title: Determine the Number of Ways to Place People II

content.problemStatement:
You receive a 2D array `points` of size `n x 2` representing integer coordinates of some points on a 2D-plane, where `points[i] = [xi, yi]`.

We define the **right** direction as positive x-axis (**increasing x-coordinate**) and the **left** direction as negative x-axis (**decreasing x-coordinate**). Similarly, we define the **up** direction as positive y-axis (**increasing y-coordinate**) and the **down** direction as negative y-axis (**decreasing y-coordinate**)

You have to place `n` people, including Evelyn and Alexander, at these points such that there is **exactly one** person at every point. Evelyn wants to be alone with Alexander, so Evelyn will build a rectangular fence with Evelyn's position as the **upper left corner** and Alexander's position as the **lower right corner** of the fence (**Note** that the fence **might not** enclose any area, i.e. it can be a line). If any person other than Evelyn and Alexander is either **inside** the fence or **on** the fence, Evelyn will be sad.

Output *the number of **pairs of points** where you can place Evelyn and Alexander, such that Evelyn **does not** become sad on building the fence*.

**Note** that Evelyn can only build a fence with Evelyn's position as the upper left corner, and Alexander's position as the lower right corner. As an example, Evelyn cannot build either of the fences in the picture below with four corners `(1, 1)`, `(1, 3)`, `(3, 1)`, and `(3, 3)`, because:

* With Evelyn at `(3, 3)` and Alexander at `(1, 1)`, Evelyn's position is not the upper left corner and Alexander's position is not the lower right corner of the fence.
* With Evelyn at `(1, 3)` and Alexander at `(1, 1)` (as the rectangle shown in the image instead of a line), Alexander's position is not the lower right corner of the fence.

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2024/01/04/example0alicebob-1.png)

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2024/01/04/example1alicebob.png)

```
Input: points = [[1,1],[2,2],[3,3]]
Output: 0
Explanation: There is no way to place Evelyn and Alexander such that Evelyn can build a fence with Evelyn's position as the upper left corner and Alexander's position as the lower right corner. Hence we return 0.
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2024/02/04/example2alicebob.png)

```
Input: points = [[6,2],[4,4],[2,6]]
Output: 2
Explanation: There are two ways to place Evelyn and Alexander such that Evelyn will not be sad:
- Place Evelyn at (4, 4) and Alexander at (6, 2).
- Place Evelyn at (2, 6) and Alexander at (4, 4).
You cannot place Evelyn at (2, 6) and Alexander at (6, 2) because the person at (4, 4) will be inside the fence.
```

**Example 3:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2024/02/04/example4alicebob.png)

```
Input: points = [[3,1],[1,3],[1,1]]
Output: 2
Explanation: There are two ways to place Evelyn and Alexander such that Evelyn will not be sad:
- Place Evelyn at (1, 1) and Alexander at (3, 1).
- Place Evelyn at (1, 3) and Alexander at (1, 1).
You cannot place Evelyn at (1, 3) and Alexander at (3, 1) because the person at (1, 1) will be on the fence.
Note that it does not matter if the fence encloses any area, the first and second fences in the image are valid.
```

**Constraints:**

* `2 <= n <= 1000`
* `points[i].length == 2`
* `-109 <= points[i][0], points[i][1] <= 109`
* All `points[i]` are distinct.
